name: Overhead line
summary: A line or route mark identifying conductors carried overhead on poles or towers rather than buried or enclosed.
description: The overhead line form identifies a circuit section strung in air between supports. On network single-line diagrams it distinguishes overhead feeders from underground cable sections, which matters because the two have different impedance, fault behaviour, auto-reclose practice and lightning exposure.

The symbol does not tell you the conductor type, span lengths, earth wire arrangement or structure type. Line data sheets and route drawings carry those. Where a feeder changes from overhead to underground, look for a cable sealing end or transition point drawn at the junction.
readingNotes: Note where the feeder changes between overhead and underground sections.
Check whether auto-reclose is applied to feeders with overhead sections.
drawingChecklist: Identify conductor type and route length.
Mark transition points to underground cable.
Reference structure and earth-wire details on route drawings.
distinction: An overhead line is strung in air; an underground cable is buried and has very different capacitance and fault characteristics.
